newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-FEYENOORD CLOSE GAP ON PSV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FEYENOORD CLOSE GAP ON PSV.

text.p: PSV's poor start to the second half of the Dutch season continued on Sunday when they lost 1-0 at Vitesse to allow Feyenoord, 2-0 winners at Volendam, to go level on points at the top of the standings.
Both sides have 48 points from 21 games, with PSV holding on to top spot on goal difference.
Twente Enschede beat Roda 3-1 on Saturday to stay third on 43 points.
PSV were knocked out of the Dutch Cup by lowly AZ Alkmaar on Wednesday and their fans' fears of another post-winter break collapse seemed justified with a poor showing on Sunday.
With several players, including Dutch leading scorer Luc Nilis, struggling for form, PSV failed to worry fourth placed Vitesse.
PSV had an early goal by Romanian midfielder Ovidiu Stinga disallowed for a push on Vitesse goalkeeper Sander Westerveld but it was a rare threat.
The goal that did count came nine minutes from time when Arco Jochemsen fired in a long range shot past PSV keeper Ronald Waterreus.
Feyenoord started furiously against Volendam, who badly missed defender Robert Molenaar, who was transferred to English club Leeds during the winter break.
The early pressure brought its reward after just four minutes when striker Henk Vos seized on a loose ball after goalkeeper Edwin Zoetebier mishandled a cross by Jen-Paul van Gastel.
However, it took Feyenoord until the last minute to find the net again, when Pablo Sanchez successfully finished off a one-two with defender George Boateng.
Ajax Amsterdam posted a confident 2-0 win over De Graafschap Doetinchem but are still a distant 15 points behind the leaders.
Jari Litmanen opened the scoring in the 51st minute when he shot home after the Graafschap defenders failed to clear.

De Graafschap, missing injured striker Eric Viscaal, battled hard but were caught out pushing up 10 minutes from time when Patrick Kluivert finished off a fast counter-attacking break by Tijani Babangida.
At the wrong end of the table RKC Waalwijk climbed off the bottom thanks to a 1-1 home draw with Groningen.
NEC Nijmegen, 3-1 losers at Willem II Tilburg, are now bottom. Both teams have 16 points from 21 matches, but NEC have an inferior goal difference.
